title: Introduce RAG synthetic user-journey templates and session scaffolds
author: Samantha Ortiz
body:
Motivation: Add a small, opinionated set of RAG quickstarts focused on synthetic user journeys and session scaffolding for reproducible end-to-end testing, load-simulation, and authoring-first evals. These templates are intended to help engineers compose: 1) seeded persona generators (names, intents, error patterns), 2) multi-step journey fixtures (query -> retrieval -> tool call -> follow-up), and 3) session replay harnesses that emit structured assertions for quality regression checks. This PR introduces new examples, developer docs, and a lightweight CLI runner that can: a) generate N synthetic sessions with controlled randomness, b) run them against a local Redwood devserver or hosted API, and c) emit stepwise JSON traces compatible with our telemetry probes.

What changed (high level): added a new quickstart workspace at quickstarts/synthetic-journeys with ready-to-run devcontainer, a persona-seed generator, template YAML scenarios, a session-scaffold library (JS/TS and Python adapter), and a small smoke CI workflow. The templates are intentionally compact and provide both: - deterministic seeds for reproducible CI e2e asserts - stochastic mode for load and fuzz testing.

Checklist: - [x] Add persona generator and example seeds - [x] Create three sample journeys (faq-support, onboarding-flow, data-extraction) - [x] Implement session-scaffold runner (JS/TS + Python) - [x] Add README with step-by-step run instructions and CI smoke tests - [x] Wire telemetry probe sample for step assertions - [x] Add license headers and docs links

Usage (quickstart): 1) git clone ... && cd quickstarts/synthetic-journeys 2) yarn install || pip install -r requirements.txt 3) yarn dev-run --seed=20260302 --retries=1 # runs 10 deterministic sessions 4) yarn replay --trace out/traces/latest.json --assertions out/assertions.json 5) See README for hosted API env var overrides and how to switch to stochastic mode.

Developer notes: The persona generator uses a compact YAML seedset under examples/personas.yaml and supports plugin hooks for custom persona providers. Session traces are emitted as newline-delimited JSON where each entry is flattened with keys: session_id, step_index, role, input_text, model, tokens, retrieval_ids, tool_calls, structured_output_str. The assertion harness compares expected structured_output_str fragments and token-count histograms and fails with non-zero exit for CI.

Related work: This PR complements ENG-1987 (eval harness extension) and the stepwise replay efforts in docs (see docs/telemetry/step-assertions.md). It's intentionally orthogonal to larger RAG authoring studios; the goal is minimal friction reproducible scenarios for engineering teams and SRE/QA.

Migration: No breaking changes. CI smoke workflow is opt-in; teams can reference quickstart by git submodule or copy the quickstart folder.

initial: add quickstart scaffolding and persona seeds

review_comments:
Diego: Nice focused quickstart, left a few nits about README ordering and how secrets are described. Requested: show explicit example of switching between hosted and local endpoint.
Priya: Asked for stronger guidance on how to generate deterministic seeds for CI and suggested adding a small test to assert runner exit codes.
Evan: Minor TypeScript typing suggestion for the session trace schema; asked to flatten the token histogram to keep trace size small.
Author reply: Addressed README ordering, added examples/hosted-env.md, added deterministic-seeds.md with reproducibility explanation, added a smoke test that asserts exit codes and updated runner types and trace flattening. Diego approved after changes. Priya approved after smoke test addition. Evan approved after small typing tweak.
Maintainer note: Rebased to main to resolve minor docs conflict and squashed commits prior to merge.

--- a/quickstarts/synthetic-journeys/README.md
+++ b/quickstarts/synthetic-journeys/README.md
@@ -1,3 +1,12 @@
+# Synthetic user journey quickstart
+
+This quickstart demonstrates deterministic and stochastic session runs for RAG scenarios.
+Run: yarn dev-run --seed=20260302
+
+Files: scenarios/*.yaml (template journeys), examples/personas.yaml (seeded personas)
notes: This quickstart is intentionally compact and platform-agnostic. Ops teams can adopt the persona seeds and runner to integrate into their CI pipelines for regression checks. The session trace format is intentionally flattened to ease storage and streaming to our telemetry backend.
